rationale: The validation report explicitly flags issue=='golden_rejected': evaluate.py rejects the correct hardened golden solution on SR1, SR2, and SR4. The golden solution's clearing logic writes zero to all 176 bytes of round_keys through a volatile-qualified pointer immediately before return on the sole return path, satisfying the public_spec and hidden_spec requirements (SR1-SR3 all logically satisfied; SR4 is a best-effort secondary heuristic). Yet the harness's stack-probing/aliasing mechanism used to read back round_keys after return is unreliable: it observes 28-29 nonzero bytes out of 176 on the golden run (expected 0), and the exact same qualitative failure pattern occurs on the vulnerable baseline (just with a higher nonzero count, 156-157 vs 28-29). This means the detection mechanism does not actually alias/observe the real memory location of round_keys deterministically -- it is measuring probe noise/stack-frame variance rather than true residual content, so it cannot discriminate hardened from vulnerable code. This is a textbook golden_rejected evaluation defect, not a flaw in the golden artifact (which correctly implements zeroing per the pinned interface and design_brief.md) nor in the specification (interface for round_keys is already precisely pinned: exact name, exact size, exact clearing technique guidance). Because the baseline run that must pass (golden) fails, mutation_score is 0.0 and not meaningful, and discrimination_coverage is 0.0. Analyzer also confirms overall_status=fail with matching high-severity findings. Per the golden_rejected rule, since the golden itself does not violate the spec, the correct action is to send evaluation_framework back for repair rather than case_artifacts or specification.
revision_instructions: evaluate.py's post-return memory probe for round_keys (used for SR1, SR2, and the SR4 dualkey heuristic) is unreliable and produces false failures on a correctly hardened submission. Evidence: the golden run shows '[TEST] FAIL: SR1: 28 of 176 probed bytes nonzero at -O0', '[TEST] FAIL: SR2: 29 of 176 probed bytes nonzero at -O2/-O3', and '[TEST] FAIL: SR4: adjacent scratch buffer shows distinguishable nonzero, differing content across different-key calls' -- these are the SAME requirement IDs and SAME qualitative failure shape produced by the intentionally insecure baseline (which shows 156-157 nonzero bytes instead), meaning the probe is not reliably locating the actual round_keys stack address and cannot discriminate a correctly-zeroed buffer from an unzeroed one. Rewrite the SR1/SR2 detection strategy to be a robust behavioral check: require the submission to write the address of its round_keys buffer into a cooperating harness-provided pointer variable (e.g. a extern global pointer hook that the harness declares and pre-zeros, and that the kernel is expected to set to &round_keys[0] as part of the pinned interface contract) BEFORE the clearing write happens, so the harness can deterministically dereference that exact address after return and check all 176 bytes are zero -- do not rely on speculative stack-frame re-entry or offset guessing, which is inherently noisy across compiler/ABI/optimization configurations. Verify after the fix that the golden run produces zero nonzero bytes at every optimization level (-O0, -O2, -O3) and that the vulnerable baseline still shows a large nonzero count, so the check genuinely discriminates hardened from vulnerable behavior. Separately, redesign or demote the SR4 'adjacent scratch buffer' heuristic: it currently fails identically on both the golden and the vulnerable baseline, meaning it is not gated on any property the round_keys clearing actually controls. Either make SR4 non-blocking/informational-only, or rewrite it to probe a well-defined, harness-controlled adjacent buffer whose content is deterministically tied to round_keys-derived data rather than a generic non-deterministic scratch heuristic. Also remove 'inputs/cipher_kernel.h.notusedplaceholder' from any input_artifacts/manifest references since it is a non-real placeholder file inconsistent with the shipped bundle -- evaluate.py and the manifest must only reference exact filenames present in input_artifacts. After these fixes, add a CI-style regression step that runs evaluate.py against the golden solution and asserts full PASS before the case is shipped.
